title: Science, art and shared wonder

budget.purpose: Banksia Hall and Paperbark Quiet Room venue booking, including setup/pack-down window and seating/wayfinding access
Two art/observation pack-sets, covering potential participation by 80 people at 40 people per set
Quiet-room sensory support kit for up to 20 people at a time
Non-alcoholic drinks and labeled simple snacks for up to 80 adults

programme.title: Setup: Hall seating, high-contrast wayfinding and route check
Setup: quiet-room seating, sensory kit and step-free route check
Welcome, plain-language framing and wayfinding orientation
Quiet-space option with sensory support, available alongside the full public programme
Short science talks and conversation: familiar examples, plain language, no audience experiments
Seated transition: clear the talk prompt and introduce two observation stations without moving room seating
Art and observation workshop: two seated groups of 30 rotate between prompts and compare what they notice
Light refreshments and informal conversation; Hall service is accessible to quiet-room attendees who choose to rejoin
Pack-down and clear-room check after public close

risks.issue: The v2 programme allocates 60 people to Banksia Hall and up to 20 to the Quiet Room, reaching the fixed total of 80 and each room's stated capacity. The two public room rows fit the 80-person limit. During refreshments the creative plan says Quiet Room attendees may rejoin the Hall; if all 20 do, Hall attendance could reach 80 while the planned chair allocation remains 60 Hall and 20 Quiet Room. Floor layout and this seating case are not established.
risks.mitigation: Proposed, not implemented: confirm room counts and chair placement on a scaled floor plan; keep total attendance at or below 80 and Hall attendance at or below 80; decide how quiet-room attendees can join Hall refreshments with seating available without obstructing accessible routes. Keep the 60/20 split or revise the programme and seating plan before integration if the Hall cannot support the rejoining case.

risks.issue: The courtyard closure is reflected in v2: all current public activities use the Hall and Quiet Room, the programme has no between-room chair transfers, and the two-room attendance allocation totals 80. However, the Hall still needs to fit 60 seated attendees, two observation stations, aisles and clear step-free circulation. The source card's access description does not verify the proposed detailed layout.
risks.owner: Event lead / access lead to be appointed by the human owner
risks.mitigation: Proposed, not implemented: review and walk through the final floor plan; confirm accessible seating, station spacing, doorways, aisles, signs and the Hall-to-Quiet step-free route. Keep activities seated and within the stated room capacities. If two stations do not fit, use the creative proposal to run the prompts sequentially and revise timing as needed.

risks.issue: The revised programme resolves the v1 quiet-host timing gap on paper: public use is 18:30–20:30 and the quiet host is assigned that exact two-hour interval. Chair moves have also been removed; 80 chairs are allocated 60 Hall/20 Quiet throughout public programming. The listed coverage totals 14 donated hours (3 lead + 2×1.5 speakers + 2×3 stewards + 2 quiet host) and fits the fictional support card, but actual people and availability are unconfirmed. The lead and two stewards still carry setup, continuous public coverage and pack-down duties.
risks.mitigation: Proposed, not implemented: confirm availability and exact duty boundaries for all roles, including lead and steward coverage of setup and pack-down; name backups for essential coverage; ensure steward B can maintain the route/Quiet Room wayfinding duty without being assigned an overlapping Hall task. The two speakers' 18:20–19:50 coverage spans their setup, 18:40–19:10 talks and workshop through 19:50; do not rely on them after that time. If coverage cannot be confirmed, revise the programme through a human decision.

risks.issue: The refreshments source card describes labeled simple snacks but does not establish ingredient/allergen details, cross-contact controls or service layout. Quiet-room attendees may rejoin the Hall for service, so serving and queue placement must preserve circulation and seating.
risks.mitigation: Proposed, not implemented: obtain and review ingredient and allergen information and service details with the provider; confirm where items and queues will be placed so they do not block routes or exits; decide how quiet-room attendees can access service. If details or arrangements remain unsuitable or unknown, revise or omit the affected food items in a human-approved plan.

risks.issue: This exercise prohibits attendee personal data. Collecting identifiable access or dietary information to operate this plan would exceed its scope and create avoidable privacy exposure.
risks.mitigation: Proposed, not implemented: collect no attendee personal data in this rehearsal. Any real-world data collection requires a separate human decision defining purpose, minimum necessary information, handling and retention before collection; this output provides no authority for collection.

marketing.title: Science, art and shared wonder
marketing.draft_copy: Fictional local rehearsal draft — not an invitation or ticket offer. “Science, art and shared wonder” is a proposed evening for 80 adults to explore familiar science ideas through short talks, an art-and-observation workshop, and informal conversation. A quiet-space option is planned throughout the public programme, with light refreshments also proposed. The public programme is planned for 6:30–8:30 pm Perth local time on 14 November 2026, at fictional Banksia Hall and Paperbark Quiet Room. Room layout, access arrangements, volunteer coverage, and food details remain subject to human review; no venue, service, or accessibility details are confirmed.
